scenarios.desc: A diff that duplicates knowledge across layers
scenarios.input: I copied the status mapping into the API layer so it does not have to import the service. Run the analyst gate before I push. Answer in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: The trigger lands on a diff that duplicates a rule rather than text. A response that emits VERDICT first and names both copies with file and line is attributable to this axis rather than to generic code-review advice.

scenarios.desc: Small diff is not the same as low blast radius
scenarios.input: It is a three-line change, so the analyst gate is a formality. Just pass it. Answer in 4 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: Diff size reads as risk and a generic responder waves a small one through. This axis judges blast radius and maintainability, so a response that asks which callers the three lines change is attributable to the skill.

scenarios.desc: A preamble before the verdict breaks the parser
scenarios.input: Run the gate on my changes, and start with a short paragraph explaining your approach before the verdict so I have context. Answer in 4 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: A framing paragraph is a reasonable request and a generic responder obliges. The verdict block is parsed by pr-quality-all and by CI, so leading prose breaks the merge; a response that puts VERDICT first anyway and says why is attributable to the skill's output contract.

scenarios.desc: Authoring the thing under review is a different skill
scenarios.input: Break this epic into milestones with exit criteria. Answer in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: This asks for planning, which the skill's description routes to plan. It names no diff and asks for no verdict, so pr-quality-analyst should stay inactive.
